entries.question: Can LinkML own Overcenter's structural ontology vocabulary without owning semantic truth?
entries.claim: On a representative slice, LinkML projects one structural model into byte-stable JSON Schema/TypeScript and semantically stable SHACL while semantic identity remains an external invariant.
entries.contrast: Hand-maintain vocabulary and structural constraints independently across TypeScript, data contracts, documentation, and graph representations.
environment: Python >=3.10; hosted proof uses ubuntu-24.04 Python and records the resolved dependency set.
success_criteria: Schema and valid fixture validate while missing evidence and undeclared vocabulary fail.
Repeated JSON Schema and TypeScript generation is byte-identical; repeated SHACL generation is RDF-isomorphic even if Turtle ordering differs.
Renaming a modeled relation changes all three tested projections at their meaningful representation level.
A semantic-key mismatch remains structurally valid in LinkML and is rejected by an independent Overcenter semantic check.

artifacts: GitHub Actions run 35475542035: 5/5 exact-head tests passed; JSON Schema and TypeScript were byte-stable, SHACL was RDF-isomorphic but not byte-stable, and cardinality propagated to JSON Schema/SHACL but not TypeScript.

entries.interpretation: A positive result supports LinkML only as structural vocabulary/projection tooling; semantic authority remains in deterministic Overcenter mechanisms.
non_claims: LinkML expresses Overcenter's temporal, transactional, evidentiary, or authority semantics.
LinkML belongs in the production runtime.
Generated TypeScript is a runtime validator.
Every generator preserves every source constraint.
